verses.1: How alone the city was when its ruler lived alone. She was like a fool. She ruled over nations, but she was nothing but a fool.
verses.2: She will weep in the night, and her pain will be unbearable. She will have no comfort from all her lovers. All her enemies will mock her.
verses.3: Judea was cast out from its land, and she suffered great hardships. She lived in foreign lands, unable to find any peace. All her enemies succeeded in defeating her.
verses.4: The paths of Zion are broken, and its doors are closed. Its priests lie down in its streets, exhausted. It is in ruins.
verses.5: They had enemies who were stronger than them. But Jehovah would judge them for their many sins. They were forced to submit to their enemies’ rule.
verses.6: And from the house of Zion, all their land was covered with snow. They had no place to rest or sleep. They walked without any strength in front of the enemy.
verses.7: Jerusalem remembered the days of its poverty and suffering. All its pleasures from ancient times were destroyed by the enemies of Israel. There was no one to save it. It saw how its people suffered under their oppression.
verses.8: Jerusalem committed a sin. As a result, all its treasures were lost. They saw its ugliness, and even she sighed and returned home.
verses.9: She forgot her past in her sorrow; she went down into the depths of despair. There’s no comfort for her. Look, God, at my suffering! How great is my wretchedness!
verses.10: Her hand spread a curse over all her offerings, because she saw nations coming from the holy place. She had ordered that they should not enter the temple.
verses.11: All the people are tired and hungry. They ask for bread, but they are given nothing to eat. Look, Lord, and see that I am a starving person.
verses.12: If not for all the hardships along the way, may you see and understand whether there is any sorrow like mine. This sorrow was brought upon me by Jehovah on that day of judgment.
verses.13: From the fire that was sent upon me, a veil fell over my feet. Then, I was restored to life again. All day long, I remained in that state.
verses.14: He will punish my sins with his hands. He will humble me on my chest. He will weaken my strength. My Lord, he has given me into his hands; I cannot stand up anymore.
verses.15: All my lords and rulers, stand before me. I command you to be gathered together in one place. Go through the gates of Jerusalem, towards the Temple of God.
verses.16: For these reasons, my eyes weep. My eyes have been brought down from the sea, as if they are far away from me. My soul is filled with sorrow. My children were once happy, but now they are in pain.
verses.17: With the tablets in her hands, she found no comfort. Jehovah commanded Jacob to go around them. Jerusalem was among their surroundings.
verses.18: The righteous is Jehovah, for he has redeemed me. May all nations hear this! May they see my suffering in my streets and in my homes. Then they will go away from me.
verses.19: I called to my lovers: “Oh, you scoundrels! You priests and elders in this city are crying out for food. They want to eat, and they want to settle their souls.”
verses.20: See, LORD, I am tired from all these hardships. My heart is broken because I have been separated from my loved ones. I am like a dead body in the house, without any hope.
verses.21: They heard that I was tired. There’s no comfort for me at all. All my enemies heard of my suffering. They were pleased because you brought about this day of judgment. It will be like yesterday.
verses.22: All their evil deeds will come before you. They will be punished just as you have punished me for all my sins. For my sorrows and my heart’s pain are too great.
